prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Generate 5 ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question, each with a short title and a description of one or two sentences. Sample the ideas from the full distribution of possible responses, and give each idea its estimated probability of being generated (a number between 0 and 1).

ideas.title: Longitudinal ATAC-seq/CUT&Tag of AP-1 footprints after transient stimulus
ideas.description: Profile chromatin accessibility and AP-1 (FOS/JUN) binding at timepoints after a transient stimulus and long after its withdrawal. Persistent AP-1-dependent open sites that outlast the signal would indicate a memory-like state.

ideas.title: Acute AP-1 degradation during the memory phase
ideas.description: Use degron (dTAG/AID) or dominant-negative (A-FOS) tools to remove AP-1 after the stimulus is gone. Then measure whether accessibility and the secondary-response transcriptional boost are lost, which would show AP-1 is needed to maintain memory rather than just to establish it.

ideas.title: Re-stimulation (priming) assays with RNA-seq
ideas.description: Compare transcriptional responses in naive versus previously stimulated cells after a rest interval of varying length. Test whether faster or stronger induction of target genes depends on AP-1 levels and occupancy.

ideas.title: Single-cell multiome and live imaging of AP-1 dynamics
ideas.description: Use single-cell RNA+ATAC, or live reporters of FOS/JUN, to follow lineages and test whether the AP-1 state is inherited through divisions and is bistable. This separates heritable memory from transient signaling.

ideas.title: Targeted AP-1 site perturbation with dCas9 and histone-mark profiling
ideas.description: Use CRISPR deletion or dCas9-based repression of specific AP-1 motifs at candidate enhancers. Pair this with H3K27ac/H3K4me1 profiling to test whether AP-1 binding is causally required for persistent enhancer marks and for the memory response at linked genes.
